Algebra I · Lesson 9.2

Factoring x² + bx + c

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Every product (x+r)(x+s)(x+r)(x+s) expands to x2+(r+s)x+rsx2+(r+s)x+rs, so factoring x2+bx+cx2+bx+c means finding two numbers with sum bb and product cc. Those are the two clues, and the product is the sharper one, since cc has only finitely many factor pairs, so the search starts there.

Problem
Two numbers have sum 1515 and product 5656. The product is the clue to search on, so list the factor pairs of 5656 and check each pair's sum. Enter the larger of the two numbers.
Show a hint
  • Starting from the product gives a shorter search. Only four pairs of whole numbers multiply to 5656, so list those pairs.
  • The pairs are 1⋅561⋅56, 2⋅282⋅28, 4⋅144⋅14 and 7⋅87⋅8. Check each sum against 1515.
Show the full solution
The factor pairs of 5656 are 1⋅561⋅56, 2⋅282⋅28, 4⋅144⋅14 and 7⋅87⋅8, with sums 5757, 3030, 1818 and 1515, so the numbers are 77 and 88, and the larger is 88​. Starting from the product kept the search short, since only four pairs needed checking.
Problem
Factor x2+8x+12x2+8x+12 as (x+r)(x+s)(x+r)(x+s). Both constants are positive, since the product and the sum are both positive. Enter the larger of the two.
Show a hint
  • Two numbers with sum 88 and product 1212. Run the factor pairs of 1212.
  • The pairs of 1212 are 1⋅121⋅12, 2⋅62⋅6 and 3⋅43⋅4. One sum is 88.
Show the full solution
The pairs of 1212 have sums 1313, 88 and 77, so the numbers are 22 and 66, giving x2+8x+12=(x+2)(x+6)x2+8x+12=(x+2)(x+6), and the larger constant is 66​. Expanding back gives x2+8x+12x2+8x+12, the check from 9.1.
Key idea
The search. To factor x2+bx+cx2+bx+c, find two numbers rr and ss with r+s=br+s=b and rs=crs=c. Then x2+bx+c=(x+r)(x+s)x2+bx+c=(x+r)(x+s), which is 9.1's forward pattern read right to left. Run the search through the factor pairs of cc, never through sums. There are endlessly many ways to write bb as a sum, but cc has only finitely many factor pairs, so listing the pairs of cc and checking each pair's sum always finishes.
Problem
Factor x2+3x−28x2+3x−28. The product of the two constants is −28−28, so they have opposite signs, and since the sum is +3+3, the positive one is larger in size. Search the pairs of 2828 with opposite signs. Enter the negative constant.
Show a hint
  • You need a factor pair of 2828 whose difference is 33, with signs chosen so the sum comes out positive.
  • The pairs of 2828 are 1⋅281⋅28, 2⋅142⋅14 and 4⋅74⋅7. Which pair has difference 33?
Show the full solution
The pair with difference 33 is 44 and 77, and the sum must be +3+3, so the positive number is 77, giving x2+3x−28=(x+7)(x−4)x2+3x−28=(x+7)(x−4), and the negative constant is −4−4​. A quick expand gives 7x−4x=3x7x−4x=3x and 7⋅(−4)=−287⋅(−4)=−28, matching the middle term and the constant.
Problem
Factor x2−13x+22x2−13x+22. The product +22+22 is positive, so the two constants share a sign, and since the sum −13−13 is negative, that shared sign is negative. Search the factor pairs of 2222, both taken negative. Enter the smaller of the two constants.
Show a hint
  • 2222 has only two factor pairs, 1⋅221⋅22 and 2⋅112⋅11, and both numbers are negative here.
  • Which pair, made negative, sums to −13−13? Then take the one farther below zero.
Show the full solution
The negative pairs are −1,−22−1,−22 with sum −23−23 and −2,−11−2,−11 with sum −13−13, so x2−13x+22=(x−2)(x−11)x2−13x+22=(x−2)(x−11), and the smaller constant is −11−11​. Writing (x+2)(x+11)(x+2)(x+11) is the standard slip, since its expansion has +13x+13x, not −13x−13x.
Key idea
Sign reasoning. Both sign facts follow from the forward pattern. A positive cc means rr and ss share a sign, and the sum of two numbers with the same sign has that sign too, so the shared sign is the sign of bb. A negative cc means rr and ss have opposite signs, and the sum of two numbers with opposite signs has the sign of the one with the larger absolute value, so that number and bb share a sign. Either way the signs are known before any list gets written, and half the candidate pairs never need checking.

The expansion x2+(r+s)x+rsx2+(r+s)x+rs has leading coefficient 11, so the two clues are only trustworthy on a quadratic whose x2x2 coefficient is also 11. Before any search, pull out the greatest common numeric factor and write it in front, where it stays. When there is no constant term, xx itself is a common factor.

Problem
Every term of 4x2+52x+1204x2+52x+120 is divisible by the same number. Pull out that greatest common numeric factor, leaving a quadratic whose x2x2 coefficient is 11, then finish the factoring. Enter the numeric factor you pulled out.
Show a hint
  • Find the largest number that divides 44, 5252 and 120120 evenly.
  • After it comes out, the search runs on x2+13x+30x2+13x+30.
Show the full solution
The greatest common factor of 44, 5252 and 120120 is 44​. It comes out first, leaving x2+13x+30x2+13x+30, which factors as (x+3)(x+10)(x+3)(x+10), so the full form is 4(x+3)(x+10)4(x+3)(x+10), with the 44 kept in front.
Problem
x2−14xx2−14x has no constant term, so both terms share the factor xx itself. Factor the expression as xx times a linear factor. Enter the constant inside the linear factor.
Show a hint
  • Write each term with an xx pulled out, x⋅xx⋅x and x⋅(−14)x⋅(−14).
  • The factorization is x(x+s)x(x+s) for one value of ss, and expanding it must give back −14x−14x.
Show the full solution
x2−14x=x(x−14)x2−14x=x(x−14), so the constant inside the linear factor is −14−14​. Expanding back gives x⋅x−14⋅xx⋅x−14⋅x, the original expression.
Key idea
Common factor first, every time. A quadratic whose x2x2 coefficient is 11 is called monic, and the two clues are the coefficients of a monic quadratic only. With a leading coefficient still in place, the constant term is no longer plainly rsrs, so the clues cannot be trusted until the common numeric factor comes out. A missing constant term means every term shares an xx, which comes out the same way and is zero at x=0x=0, a root worth keeping once the lesson turns to equations. Skipping this first step is the most common practical error in factoring.

When b=0b=0 the sum clue is r+s=0r+s=0, so s=−rs=−r and the product is −r2−r2. That is why x2−49x2−49 factors as (x+7)(x−7)(x+7)(x−7), the conjugate identity from 9.1 run backwards, with the cross terms cancelling. The marks to recognize are a missing middle term and a negative perfect square constant.

Problem
Compute 532−472532−472 without working out either square. The difference of squares pattern applies to plain numbers too, and it turns the subtraction into one easy multiplication. Enter the value.
Show a hint
  • The conjugate identity from 9.1, a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b)a2−b2=(a+b)(a−b), applies with a=53a=53 and b=47b=47.
  • (53−47)(53+47)=6⋅100(53−47)(53+47)=6⋅100.
Show the full solution
532−472=(53−47)(53+47)=6⋅100=600532−472=(53−47)(53+47)=6⋅100=600​. Running the identity in reverse replaced two squarings and a subtraction with one easy product, and the direct arithmetic agrees, 2809−2209=6002809−2209=600.
Fun fact
In 1977 Ron Rivest, Adi Shamir and Leonard Adleman built RSA encryption on a lopsided fact. Multiplying two enormous numbers is quick, but no fast method is known for recovering the factors from the product. Much of internet security rests on that gap.
Problem
The quadratic x2+18x+81x2+18x+81 is the search's r=sr=s case, since 81=9281=92 and 1818 is twice 99, so it factors as (x+9)2(x+9)2. Now change the constant to 8282. Run the full search for x2+18x+82x2+18x+82 and answer yes or no. Does it factor with integer constants?
Show a hint
  • Both numbers would have to be positive, since the sum and the product are both positive. List every factor pair of 8282.
  • 82=1⋅82=2⋅4182=1⋅82=2⋅41, and those are all the pairs. Check both sums against 1818.
Show the full solution
The pairs of 8282 are 1⋅821⋅82 and 2⋅412⋅41, with sums 8383 and 4343, and negative pairs have negative sums, so the search comes up empty and the answer is nono​. An empty search is a proof, since the pairs are all there is to check.
Key idea
Two shortcuts and one honest limit. A missing middle term with a negative square constant means a difference of squares, x2−k2=(x+k)(x−k)x2−k2=(x+k)(x−k). A constant that is a perfect square, with bb twice its root, means a perfect square trinomial, the r=sr=s case of the search, x2+2kx+k2=(x+k)2x2+2kx+k2=(x+k)2. And because cc has finitely many factor pairs, an empty search is a proof, not a failure. When every pair is checked and none has sum bb, no integer factorization exists. Quadratics like that are handled in chapter 11.

Once the left side of x2+bx+c=0x2+bx+c=0 is factored, it is a product equal to zero, and by the zero product property from 9.1 at least one of the factors is zero. Each factor set to zero is a linear equation. The property applies to a product equal to zero and nothing else, so put zero on one side before splitting anything.

Problem
Solve x2−4x−45=0x2−4x−45=0. Factor the left side, then the zero product property splits the equation into two linear ones. Enter the positive root.
Show a hint
  • Two numbers with product −45−45 and sum −4−4. The signs differ, and the negative one is larger in size.
  • The pair is −9−9 and 55, so the factors are x−9x−9 and x+5x+5.
Show the full solution
x2−4x−45=(x−9)(x+5)x2−4x−45=(x−9)(x+5), so x=9x=9 or x=−5x=−5, and the positive root is 99​. Checking, 81−36−45=081−36−45=0.
Problem
Solve x(x+5)=24x(x+5)=24. The left side is already factored, but the right side is not zero, so neither factor is forced to equal anything. Expand, move every term to one side, and factor again before splitting. Enter the positive root.
Show a hint
  • The zero product property only works on a product equal to zero. Expand and subtract 2424 first.
  • x2+5x−24=0x2+5x−24=0 needs two numbers with sum 55 and product −24−24.
Show the full solution
Expanding gives x2+5x−24=0x2+5x−24=0, which factors as (x+8)(x−3)(x+8)(x−3), so x=−8x=−8 or x=3x=3, and the positive root is 33​. The check runs against the original equation, 3⋅8=243⋅8=24. Splitting x(x+5)=24x(x+5)=24 into x=24x=24 or x+5=24x+5=24 is exactly the trap 9.1 named.
Key idea
The full pipeline. Rearrange until one side is zero. Pull out the common numeric factor, and xx itself if there is no constant term. Run the search on the monic quadratic that remains, signs settled first. Split with the zero product property. Then check one root in the original equation, the habit from 9.1. Substituting x=3x=3 into x(x+5)=24x(x+5)=24 gives 3⋅8=243⋅8=24, the original statement back again, so the pair was right.

You can now factor any quadratic that turns into x2+bx+cx2+bx+c once a numeric factor comes out, whenever an integer pair exists, and solve the equations built from those factorizations. Two things are still out of reach, a leading coefficient that does not divide out, and a quadratic whose search comes up empty.

Problem
A poster is 66 inches taller than it is wide, and its area is 187187 square inches. Writing ww for the width gives w(w+6)=187w(w+6)=187. Rearrange, factor and split. Both roots solve the equation, but only one can be a width. Enter the width in inches.
Show a hint
  • Expand and move 187187 over, then search for two numbers with sum 66 and product −187−187.
  • 187=11⋅17187=11⋅17, and 17−11=617−11=6.
Show the full solution
w2+6w−187=0w2+6w−187=0 factors as (w+17)(w−11)(w+17)(w−11), so w=−17w=−17 or w=11w=11, and a width is a positive length, so the width in inches is 1111​. The check is the original statement, 11⋅17=18711⋅17=187, an 1111 by 1717 inch poster.
Problem
Factor 3x2−45x+1503x2−45x+150 completely. The common numeric factor comes out first. The quadratic left behind has a positive constant and a negative middle term, so both constants in its factored form are negative. Enter the smaller of the two.
Show a hint
  • Divide 33 out of every term, then search x2−15x+50x2−15x+50 among negative pairs only.
  • Which factor pair of 5050, both taken negative, sums to −15−15?
Show the full solution
Pulling out 33 leaves x2−15x+50x2−15x+50, and the negative pair with sum −15−15 and product 5050 is −5−5 and −10−10, so 3x2−45x+150=3(x−5)(x−10)3x2−45x+150=3(x−5)(x−10), and the smaller constant is −10−10​. Dropping the 33 when writing the complete factorization is the standard slip, it stays in front.

Every quadratic here began monic or became monic after a numeric factor came out. When the leading coefficient stays, as in 2x2+7x+32x2+7x+3, the sum and product clues are no longer enough on their own. Lesson 9.3, Factoring ax2+bx+cax2+bx+c, extends the search to that case.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Two numbers have sum 1616 and product 3939. Enter the larger one.
Show the solution
The factor pairs of 3939 have sums 4040 and 1616, so the numbers are 33 and 1313, and the larger is 1313​.
Practice
Factor x2+10x+16x2+10x+16. Enter the smaller of the two constants in the factored form.
Show the solution
The pair with sum 1010 is 22 and 88, so x2+10x+16=(x+2)(x+8)x2+10x+16=(x+2)(x+8), and the smaller constant is 22​.
Practice
Factor x2+15x+36x2+15x+36. Enter the larger of the two constants in the factored form.
Show the solution
The pair with sum 1515 is 33 and 1212, so x2+15x+36=(x+3)(x+12)x2+15x+36=(x+3)(x+12), and the larger constant is 1212​.
Practice
Factor x2+2x−48x2+2x−48. The two constants in the factors differ in sign. Enter the negative one.
Show the solution
The pair of 4848 with difference 22 is 66 and 88, with the 88 positive, so x2+2x−48=(x+8)(x−6)x2+2x−48=(x+8)(x−6), and the negative constant is −6−6​.
Practice
Factor x2−12x+35x2−12x+35. Both constants are negative. Enter the smaller of the two.
Show the solution
The negative pair with sum −12−12 is −5−5 and −7−7, so x2−12x+35=(x−5)(x−7)x2−12x+35=(x−5)(x−7), and the smaller constant is −7−7​.
Practice
Factor 7x2+42x+357x2+42x+35 completely, pulling out the greatest common numeric factor first. Enter the larger of the two constants in the factored form.
Show the solution
The common factor is 77, and pulling it out leaves x2+6x+5=(x+1)(x+5)x2+6x+5=(x+1)(x+5), so 7x2+42x+35=7(x+1)(x+5)7x2+42x+35=7(x+1)(x+5) and the larger constant is 55​. Without the pull the search on 7x27x2 never even starts, since the pattern needs a plain x2x2.
Practice
Factor x2−22xx2−22x as xx times a linear factor. Enter the constant inside the linear factor.
Show the solution
x2−22x=x(x−22)x2−22x=x(x−22), so the constant inside the linear factor is −22−22​.
Practice
x2−225x2−225 fits the form x2+bx+cx2+bx+c with b=0b=0 and c=−225c=−225. Factor it as (x+k)(x−k)(x+k)(x−k) and enter the positive integer kk.
Show the solution
The pair must multiply to −225−225 and add to 00, so it is 1515 and −15−15, giving x2−225=(x+15)(x−15)x2−225=(x+15)(x−15) and k=15k=15​.
Practice
Compute 292−212292−212 in your head, as a difference times a sum. Enter the value.
Show the solution
292−212=(29−21)(29+21)=8⋅50=400292−212=(29−21)(29+21)=8⋅50=400​. The sum does not have to be a power of ten for the shortcut to be quick.
Practice
x2−32x+256x2−32x+256 is a perfect square trinomial, (x+r)2(x+r)2 for one value of rr. Enter rr, sign included.
Show the solution
256=162256=162 and −32−32 is twice −16−16, so x2−32x+256=(x−16)2x2−32x+256=(x−16)2 and r=−16r=−16​. This is the search's r=sr=s case, the pair −16−16 and −16−16.
Practice
Does x2−7x−44x2−7x−44 factor with integer constants? Run the factor pairs of 4444 with opposite signs and answer yes or no.
Show the solution
The pair with difference 77 is 44 and 1111, with the 1111 negative, so x2−7x−44=(x−11)(x+4)x2−7x−44=(x−11)(x+4), and the answer is yesyes​.
Practice
Solve x2−3x−70=0x2−3x−70=0. Enter the larger root.
Show the solution
x2−3x−70=(x−10)(x+7)x2−3x−70=(x−10)(x+7), so x=10x=10 or x=−7x=−7, and the larger root is 1010​. Checking, 100−30−70=0100−30−70=0.
Practice
Solve x2=8x+65x2=8x+65. Move every term to one side before factoring. Enter the negative root.
Show the solution
Rearranging gives x2−8x−65=0x2−8x−65=0, which factors as (x−13)(x+5)=0(x−13)(x+5)=0, so x=13x=13 or x=−5x=−5, and the negative root is −5−5​. Checking in the original, 25=−40+6525=−40+65.
Practice
Solve x2=19xx2=19x. Do not divide both sides by xx, since a root is lost that way. Enter the smaller root.
Show the solution
x2−19x=0x2−19x=0 factors as x(x−19)=0x(x−19)=0, so x=0x=0 or x=19x=19, and the smaller root is 00​. Dividing by xx at the start loses exactly this root.
Practice
Solve 3x2+27x+42=03x2+27x+42=0. Pull out the common factor first. Both roots are negative. Enter the larger one.
Show the solution
Dividing out 33 gives x2+9x+14=(x+2)(x+7)=0x2+9x+14=(x+2)(x+7)=0, so x=−2x=−2 or x=−7x=−7, and the larger root is −2−2​. On the number line −2−2 is to the right of −7−7.
Practice
Two pages of a book have consecutive page numbers that multiply to 306306. Consecutive numbers give n(n+1)=306n(n+1)=306. Solve it, reject the root that cannot be a page number, and enter the smaller page number.
Show the solution
n2+n−306=0n2+n−306=0 factors as (n+18)(n−17)(n+18)(n−17), so n=17n=17 or n=−18n=−18, and a page number is positive, so the pages are 1717 and 1818 and the smaller is 1717​. The check is the original statement, 17⋅18=30617⋅18=306.
Practice
Solve 2x2−338=02x2−338=0. The common factor comes out first, and what remains is a difference of squares. Enter the negative root.
Show the solution
Dividing out 22 gives x2−169=(x+13)(x−13)=0x2−169=(x+13)(x−13)=0, so x=13x=13 or x=−13x=−13, and the negative root is −13−13​. Checking, 2⋅169−338=02⋅169−338=0.
